request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rollover now soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open. All 4 tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What changed:** in `RollOver.java`, after the `ROLLOVER` audit line is written, the rollover takes the old year's periods in start-date order. It re-reads each one from the store and skips any that are already closed or soft-closed. Each remaining period is soft-closed the same way a manual soft close does it, through `PeriodClosing.fixNow` with soft on, and gets its own `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED sheet=… by=… period=… total=…` line. These are written in the same transaction as the rest of the rollover. I also updated the description comments in `RollOver.java` and `rollover.POST.yml` to match.

**One thing to decide:** undoing a rollover doesn't reopen these soft-closed periods. It still only removes the new periods and takes back the opening balances. The request didn't mention undo, so I left it alone; if undo should also reverse the soft closes, that's a separate change.
